title: Hurricane Irma-In the eye of the storm
description: Kathleen McFarland and Sarah Linsalato from Wolcott, CT tell there story of surviving Hurricane Irma on St. Maarten. They were rescued by the New York Air National Guard's 106th Rescue Wing on September 9th, 2017.
credit: Staff Sgt. Erin Mills, Senior Airman Moshe Paul, Airman 1st Class Codie Trimble, Staff Sgt. Zach Vaughn

transcript.text: (thunder crashing)
(light orchestral music)
- We were in St. Martin on vacation,
my niece, my girlfriend, we were just there to have
a good time, we knew about the hurricane when we
got there, and it was very questionable as to
what it was going to do, they didn't really
know what was going to happen.
It was probably Tuesday, where it really started
getting serious as too, this is going to be a
problem folks, and we need to batten down the hatches
and we need to make a plan, and we were awoken at
4 o'clock in the morning by very, very strong winds,
and it got bad to worse quickly.
- The water had already started to flood underneath
the screen door, the slider door, and that was just
due to the rain, because we were high up, we weren't
anywhere near the ocean.
And when the roof came off of the living room
of our unit, we were all in there, my aunt and I
just missed getting hit by the roof as it was coming down.
So we ran into the bedroom, we were instructed then
if there had been any serious damage, to call the
front desk and let them know.
They told us to get into the bathroom, the bathroom
had already been compromised, so we went into the bedroom,
the room was shaking, we knew it wasn't safe in there,
I said, you know, I don't mean to be dramatic,
but I think we'd better get under the mattress,
and we did, not long after we got under the mattress
of the bed in the bedroom, that's when that roof gave away.
- Thank goodness there was in indoor stairwell,
and we we're able to escape down in to that.
We were there, it was probably a good 45 minutes an hour,
waiting out that part of the storm.
Debris, I could see flying, flying by, and I didn't
want to say anything because I didn't wanna scare the
kids, so I kept that to myself, and we got our wits
about us when the storm was over, and we headed right
down to the lobby.
All of the staff, within 24 hours, they were on grounds,
taking care of us, the best they could, they took our
names and passport numbers right away, and started
making lists, when we got into the lobby, there was
water, there was snacks, and people were there that
you could talk too, they brought us into the visitor
center, and put us on buses and they brought us to
the airport, and not too long after that an American
plane landed.
Love every, every, every member of the military that
helped us, because I wouldn't be alive right now,
I believe that because of the stories that we have heard
afterwards of the devastation, the desperation,
the things that people are doing,
I wouldn't be alive if our US government hadn't
come and gotten us.
And I have a whole new appreciation,
whole new appreciation, I mean it,
I come up to you all and I shake your hands,
what I really want to do is just kiss you right on the lips.
(laughing)
(upbeat pop music)
- The airport was destroyed but cleaned up enough
to obviously get military planes to come in and rescue
us, there was...
Had to of been 500 to a thousand people in line ahead of us,
we got a little discouraged, we didn't think we were going
to get off, and then we saw American planes and I have
never seen a more beautiful sight in my life as that flag.
- So we were at the airport, a good probably three hours,
they were mobilizing many of planes, of course moms,
babies, they were getting on the first planes,
my understanding is, is we got on the last one that day.
Just the feeling, just oh my god, were getting out of here.
I can't even put it into words, I swelled, I swelled
to wanting too burst.
- When we finally were able to walk to the plane,
it was the best feeling in my life, as we approached
the wind, was deafening, the sand was hitting us,
it felt like little needles, I loved every second of it.
When I boarded that plane, I knew then, I was going
to see my children and my husband again.
- Got on that plane willingly and listened to that noise
and just couldn't stop smiling, we did a selfie right
at that moment of the three of us, and you can't even
see my eyes, its ear to ear...
And then we took the 45 minute flight over here with
a great group of folks, great group of folks,
they really watched out for us, even when we got here
to the airport, got through some Red Cross, some snacks,
some people with some things to do, I knew that I needed
to come to the Sheraton, so I came out and there
was military at the airport door, each and every one
of us, where do you need to go?
They brought us to our hotels, they not only brought
us to our hotels, they waiting just to make sure that
we could secure rooms.
And that's the story, that's the story.
(light orchestral music)
